title: Records
hook: A record is a type whose job is data: value equality, with-copies, and a printable shape. Auth tokens and Redis DTOs fit. Your SQS worker host does not.

sections.heading: record class versus record struct
sections.prose: record or record class is a reference type with value equality: two instances are equal if their types match and their fields compare equal, even if they are different objects. record struct is a value type with the same equality story and copies on assignment. Neither replaces IDisposable services. Record classes can inherit from other record classes; record structs cannot inherit. Positional records (record AuthToken(string Sub, string Iss)) generate a primary constructor, init properties, Deconstruct, and formatted ToString.

sections.heading: with-expressions and immutability
sections.prose: with creates a new instance copying the original and overlaying named properties. It does not mutate. That is how you mint a token with a refreshed expiry without touching the one sitting in a cache. init properties plus required (module 04) keep construction honest. If you add a set accessor, you have a mutable record — legal, but you just lost the “safe to use as a dictionary key” story (next topic).

snippets.label: Auth token and Redis DTO records
snippets.explanation: AuthToken is a reference record with value equality — good for tests and for comparing claims. RedisEntry is a readonly record struct so cache metadata stays a value. with copies; token is unchanged.

sections.heading: When not to use a record
sections.prose: Entities with identity (the same attempt id, mutating score) are classes with reference equality, or you override equality carefully. Records that contain mutable lists still compare list contents by default in generated equality, which can surprise you. For API boundaries, positional records are concise; for versioning, named properties and explicit [property: Json*] attributes stay readable. Equality and GetHashCode details are the next page — do not stop at “records are equal by value.”

interviewTakeaways: record class: heap object, value equality. record struct: copy, value equality.
with is nondestructive copy, not mutation.
Positional records generate constructor, init properties, Deconstruct, ToString.
commonPitfalls: Using a mutable record as a dictionary key.
Expecting record inheritance to work on record struct.
